literature_notes: L1 is the only ledger line. It reports a FLAG-tagged CPD construct expressed in HEK293 cells, but it names no residue, no loop, and no terminus for the insertion site. The detection protocol (fixation + 0.5% Triton X-100 permeabilization before antibody staining) gives intracellular access, so the experiment is equally consistent with a cytoplasmic tag as with a surface tag — it does not confirm extracellular display. The topology_derived rule requires that the paper reports a tagged construct AND that exactly one terminus is extracellular, allowing the position to be computed from the landmarks. CPD is a type-I single-pass protein whose extracellular N-terminus (mature residue 32) is the only extracellular terminus, but the permeabilization-based protocol in L1 does not establish that the FLAG tag faces the extracellular space rather than the cytoplasm (intracellular C-tail, residues 1321–1380, is also a common tag location). Because the face of the tag is unknown and no position is named, topology_derived cannot be applied. No other ledger line exists. Zero sites qualify.
